sections.title: Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Child-Friendly Safety Planning

content.title: Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Child-Friendly Safety Planning
content.overview: This section provides a trauma-informed, practical guide to understanding the core purpose of child-friendly safety planning and how it shapes physical, emotional, and relational safety in daily family life. Designed for parents, caregivers, and family support practitioners, it focuses on realistic, repeatable steps that strengthen safety, predictability, and connection.
content.psychoeducation: Why does child-friendly safety planning matter in section 1? Children and families thrive on predictability, nervous-system safety, and attuned repair. When child-friendly safety planning is practised consistently, stress responses decrease and relational trust grows. Why child friendly safety planning matters for child development.
learning_goals: Understand the purpose and value of child friendly safety planning. (Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Child-Friendly Safety Planning)
Identify common challenges and how to respond calmly. (Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Child-Friendly Safety Planning)
Practice simple, repeatable strategies that build confidence. (Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Child-Friendly Safety Planning)
Strengthen connection and emotional safety during difficult moments. (Foundations & Baseline Understanding: Child-Friendly Safety Planning)
step_by_step: Pause & Ground: Notice your own breathing, body tension, and tone before addressing child-friendly safety planning.
Observe Factually: Notice what is happening in the moment around child-friendly safety planning without blame or judgement.
Connect & Validate: Acknowledge feelings and safety needs clearly and calmly.
Respond Simply: Choose one clear, age-appropriate action or boundary for child-friendly safety planning.
Reflect & Repair: Review what worked, repair any rupture honestly, and record your next small step.
parent_scripts: "I can see this moment feels big right now. Let's slow down and take one step together with child-friendly safety planning."
"Everyone is safe here. We can talk about what happened and work out the next step calmly."
"I noticed I was getting stressed. I'm taking a breath so I can listen properly."
"We don't have to get everything perfect today — we are practising child-friendly safety planning one routine at a time."
practical_examples: Everyday Routine: Applying child-friendly safety planning during a busy morning or bedtime transition by slowing down, offering two calm choices, and keeping tone steady.
Moment of Stress: When tension rises around child-friendly safety planning, pausing for 10 seconds before speaking, validating feelings, and focusing on safety first.
Follow-Through & Review: Recording a factual note after practising child-friendly safety planning to notice what helped the child settle and what support would help next time.
reflection_questions: What part of child friendly safety planning feels easiest for me?
What part feels hardest, and why?
How did my own childhood shape my reactions?
What is one small change I can try this week?
practice_ideas: Try a 2-minute grounding exercise before responding to your child.
Practice naming emotions using simple, non-judgemental language.
Role-play a challenging moment and rehearse a calm script.
Identify one routine where child friendly safety planning can be used daily.
content.closing_message: Progress in child-friendly safety planning comes from small, consistent moments of safety, honesty, and repair — not perfection. Every time you pause, stay regulated, and choose a safer response, you build lasting trust.

content_variants.toddlers: For babies & toddlers (0–4): Focus on gentle tone, physical comfort, predictable routines, and simple 3-to-5 word reassurance while practising child-friendly safety planning.
content_variants.school_age: For school-age children (5–11): Use clear explanations, visual routines, curiosity about their feelings, and collaborative problem-solving around child-friendly safety planning.
content_variants.teens: For adolescents (12–18): Respect autonomy, listen without lecturing, agree on clear safety boundaries, and involve teens in decisions about child-friendly safety planning.
content_variants.fatherhood: For fathers & male caregivers: Model calm accountability, steady emotional presence, and non-frightening leadership when practising child-friendly safety planning.

red_flags: Immediate physical danger, threats, intimidation, or coercive control observed during child-friendly safety planning.
A child shows fear, freezing, dissociation, or disclosure of harm related to child-friendly safety planning.
An adult is unable to regulate or maintain safe supervision while attempting child-friendly safety planning.
Signs of acute mental health crisis or substance intoxication affecting child safety.
when_to_escalate: Pause learning immediately if anyone is in danger and use verified emergency or crisis supports.
Follow jurisdiction-specific child protection and mandatory reporting obligations when harm is disclosed or suspected.
Engage a qualified supervisor, specialist DFV practitioner, or clinician when risk exceeds self-directed learning.

trauma_informed.clinical: Nervous-system lens for child-friendly safety planning: Recognises fight, flight, freeze, and fawn survival responses, window of tolerance, and the need for co-regulation before cognitive problem-solving.
trauma_informed.relational: Attachment lens for child-friendly safety planning: Prioritises connection before correction, attunement to cues, shame-free accountability, and timely repair after ruptures.
trauma_informed.justice: Fairness & cultural lens for child-friendly safety planning: Respects cultural strengths, kinship networks, neurodiversity, disability access, and structural barriers without equating poverty with neglect.
trauma_informed.fatherhood: Accountable fatherhood lens for child-friendly safety planning: Replaces control or withdrawal with steady, reliable care, honest repair, and child-centred safety.

sections.simplified_parent_version:
What child-friendly safety planning means:
Child-Friendly Safety Planning is about keeping daily life safe, calm, and predictable so your child feels supported and understood.

How to practise it:
1. Pause and take one slow breath first.
2. Notice what your child needs right now.
3. Use a calm voice and one clear step.
4. Repair kindly if things go off track.
